walkthroughs.body_html:
The Challenge of Natural Hazards — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Challenge of Natural Hazards brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Challenge of Natural Hazards.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

27 degrees

15 degrees

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.

mcqs.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
options: Waves erode cliffs by pushing water against the rock until it breaks.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
Through hydraulic action (water compressing air in cracks), abrasion (waves throwing rocks against cliffs), attrition (rocks smashing against each other), and solution.
